fetched_pages.title: Fallback fields
fetched_pages.content:
Use fallback fields to handle document variations in a document type. If a field fails to extract data, you can specify a backup, or fallback field to extract the same data using a different method. To specify fallbacks between fields, specify consecutive fields that use the same ID.

Fallbacks enable you to use a single config to extract data from similar documents whose formatting can vary. For example, say you want to extract a "total amount" field that appears in a table in document revision A and in a free-text paragraph in document revision B. You can define two fields in one configuration with the same ID (total_amount), which use the Row method and the Query Group method, respectively.

A field evaluates as "failed" and falls back if it returns an empty array, null, or undefined. A field evaluates to "passed" and doesn't fall back if it returns an empty string or 0. Fallback fields can be of any kind. For example, you can fall back from a field, to a computed field, to a section group.

Limitations:
- Fallbacks don't work across nested objects.
- Fallbacks don't work within a Query Group method.

Example 1: consecutive fields with same ID using different anchors/methods.
Example 2: LLM prompt fallbacks using anchors to force null returns and trigger fallback.

fetched_pages.title: Field query object
fetched_pages.content:
A field is the basic SenseML query unit for extracting a piece of document data. The output of a field is a JSON key-value pair.

Key parameters include:
- id (required): Sensible uses the ID as the key in the structured key/value output (parsed_document object). If a field fails and returns null, you can specify a fallback field with the same ID.
- anchor: For layout-based methods, required — matched text that narrows down the location of the target data. For LLM-based methods, optional — if the matched text is present anywhere in the document, Sensible runs the method on the whole document, otherwise it returns null.
- method (required): defines how to extract target data.
- type: the data type to extract.
- match: first, last, all, allWithNull, mostFrequent — specifies which anchor to use when there are multiple matches.

fetched_pages.title: Accuracy measures
fetched_pages.content:
You can measure the accuracy of data that Sensible extracts from a document in the following ways:
- Logical validations: Write validations in JsonLogic to check that fields meet your conditions (e.g., return errors if a quoted rate is null).
- OCR confidence scores: Get a score for the quality of text images.
- Confidence signals: For LLM-extracted data, Sensible asks the LLM to report uncertainties.
- Extraction coverage: A score measuring how fully an extraction captured all data. It's a percentage comparing non-null, validated fields to total fields returned by a config. For example, a coverage score of 70% with no validation errors means 30% of fields were null.
